prediction.rationale:
Cooler: reduced efficiency. Evidence: TS4 mean temperature 39.7 °C (28% above healthy); TS1 mean temperature 44.1 °C (23% above healthy); TS3 mean temperature 46.4 °C (19% above healthy). Thermal dissipation is sub-optimal, allowing gradual temperature elevation during continuous load cycles.
Valve: optimal. Evidence: PS2 pressure rise time 9.39 s (within 1% of healthy); PS1/PS2 valve switching lag 9.86 s (within 1% of healthy). Valve switching latency remains tightly within normal healthy tolerances.
Pump leakage: severe leakage. Evidence: FS1 mean volume flow 6.36 l/min (3% below healthy); EPS1/FS1 power-to-flow ratio 391 W·min/l (within 2% of healthy); SE system efficiency factor 56.3 % (4% below healthy). High power-to-flow ratio demonstrates extensive internal leakage across the pump chambers.
Accumulator: severely reduced. Evidence: PS2 pressure ripple 46.3 bar (within 1% of healthy). Marked pressure ripple and reduced peak pressure indicate severe loss of hydraulic accumulator gas pre-charge.

tslm_prediction.rationale:
Cooler: reduced efficiency. Evidence: TS4 mean temperature 39.7 °C (28% above healthy); TS1 mean temperature 44.1 °C (22% above healthy); TS3 mean temperature 46.3 °C (19% above healthy). Moderate fluid temperature rise and diminished heat exchange indicate degraded cooler efficiency.
Valve: small lag. Evidence: PS1/PS2 valve switching lag 9.88 s (within 1% of healthy); PS2 pressure rise time 9.46 s (within 2% of healthy). Hydraulic valve exhibits slight transient lag while maintaining target pressure.
Pump leakage: weak leakage. Evidence: FS1 mean volume flow 6.47 l/min (within 2% of healthy); EPS1/FS1 power-to-flow ratio 382 W·min/l (within 1% of healthy); SE system efficiency factor 57.7 % (within 1% of healthy). Volumetric delivery is slightly compromised due to minor internal bypass flow.
Accumulator: severely reduced. Evidence: PS2 pressure ripple 46.5 bar (within 1% of healthy). Pressure buffering is largely ineffective due to compromised pre-charge pressure in the accumulator.
